note: Hand-labeled ground truth for extraction category accuracy evaluation based on ASVS 5.0.0. Labels follow the TSD-anchored definition: 'design' means verifiable from the Technical Specification Document alone (architecture, data flows, trust boundaries, rules/policies). Extend this set for broader coverage.

category_definitions.design: TSD-verifiable: architecture, data classification, trust boundaries, defined limits/rules, encryption strategy, access control model
category_definitions.code: Requires source code inspection: algorithm work factors, exact parsing/sanitization logic, cookie flags, parameterized queries, OTP entropy
category_definitions.infrastructure: Requires ops/config audit: CI/CD, deployment pipelines, HTTP header values, TLS cipher testing, dependency version checks, server accounts
category_definitions.process: Requires organizational assessment: SDLC policy, threat modeling cadence, cryptographic inventory maintenance, SBOM maintenance

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that cryptographic discovery mechanisms are employed to identify all instances of cryptography in the system
items.rationale: Employing discovery mechanisms across the enterprise is an organizational process.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that a cryptographic inventory is maintained. This must include a documented plan that outlines the migration path
items.rationale: Maintaining an ongoing inventory and migration plan is a continuous organizational process, not a static software property.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that an inventory catalog, such as software bill of materials (SBOM), is maintained of all third-party libraries in use
items.rationale: Continuous SBOM maintenance falls under organizational supply chain procedures.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application only contains components which have not breached the documented update and remediation time frames.
items.rationale: Remediation SLAs and component lifecycle management are governance and organizational processes.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that security controls are in place to prevent browsers from rendering content or functionality... using the attachment disposition type in the Content-Disposition header
items.rationale: HTTP response headers like Content-Disposition are typically server or API gateway configuration details.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that a Strict-Transport-Security header field is included on all responses to enforce an HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) policy.
items.rationale: HSTS is a server configuration detail, not verifiable strictly from a TSD.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) Access-Control-Allow-Origin header field is a fixed value by the application
items.rationale: CORS headers are web server or gateway configurations.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that HTTP responses include a Content-Security-Policy response header field which defines directives to ensure the browser only loads and executes trusted content
items.rationale: CSP HTTP headers require inspecting live server configurations.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application sets a referrer policy to prevent leakage... using the Referrer-Policy HTTP response header field
items.rationale: Referrer-Policy is an infrastructure-level HTTP header configuration.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the web application uses the frame-ancestors directive of the Content-Security-Policy header field for every HTTP response
items.rationale: Specific CSP directives are tested against live server responses.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the Content-Security-Policy header field specifies a location to report violations.
items.rationale: CSP reporting endpoint configuration is managed at the server/infrastructure level.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that all HTTP responses that initiate a document rendering... include the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header field
items.rationale: COOP is an HTTP response header verified through server config or dynamic testing.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that every HTTP response with a message body contains a Content-Type header field that matches the actual content
items.rationale: Content-Type mappings are handled by web server configurations.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that only user-facing endpoints... automatically redirect from HTTP to HTTPS
items.rationale: HTTP to HTTPS redirects are managed at the load balancer or web server.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that only HTTP methods that are explicitly supported by the application... can be used and that unused methods are blocked.
items.rationale: Blocking unused HTTP verbs is a standard web server or WAF configuration.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that default user accounts (e.g., “root”, “admin”, or “sa”) are not present in the application or are disabled.
items.rationale: Verifying the absence of default OS or database accounts requires a live operational audit.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that only the latest recommended versions of the TLS protocol are enabled, such as TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.
items.rationale: TLS protocol version configurations are entirely infrastructure-dependent.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that proper certification revocation, such as Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) Stapling, is enabled and configured.
items.rationale: OCSP stapling is a web server or reverse proxy TLS configuration.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that an encrypted protocol such as TLS is used for all inbound and outbound connections... The server must not fall back to insecure or unencrypted protocols.
items.rationale: Enforcing TLS across network boundaries is a deployment/infrastructure policy.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that a secrets management solution, such as a key vault, is used to securely create, store, control access to, and destroy backend secrets.
items.rationale: Integration of a key vault is an infrastructure deployment configuration.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application is deployed either without any source control metadata, including the .git or .svn folders, or in a way that these folders are inaccessible
items.rationale: Restricting access to deployment artifacts relies on CI/CD rules and web server config.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that debug modes are disabled for all components in production environments
items.rationale: Disabling debug modes is an environment-specific deployment configuration.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application does not expose detailed version information of backend components.
items.rationale: Suppressing server banner versions (like Server or X-Powered-By) is a server hardening task.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application prevents sensitive data from being cached in server components, such as load balancers and application caches
items.rationale: Cache configuration at the load balancer or proxy layer is an infrastructure concern.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application’s documentation defines input validation rules for how to check the validity of data items against an expected structure.
items.rationale: Defining validation schemas is a core design specification found in a TSD.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application’s documentation defines how to validate the logical and contextual consistency of combined data items
items.rationale: Business logic rules and combined data checks are defined during architectural design.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that expectations for business logic limits and validations are documented
items.rationale: Business capacity limits must be documented in a specification document.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application is designed to enforce input validation at a trusted service layer.
items.rationale: The choice of where validation occurs (trusted layer vs client-side) is an architectural decision.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that high-value business logic flows require multi-user approval to prevent unauthorized or accidental actions.
items.rationale: Multi-user approval workflows are high-level design choices visible in a TSD.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that application documentation states the expected security features that browsers using the application must support
items.rationale: Documenting browser security expectations is a TSD-level policy requirement.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the documentation defines the permitted file types, expected file extensions, and maximum size
items.rationale: Specifying allowed file extensions and sizes is an explicit design policy.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that application documentation defines how controls such as rate limiting, anti-automation, and adaptive response, are used
items.rationale: Documenting the anti-automation policy is a TSD responsibility.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that a list of context-specific words is documented in order to prevent their use in passwords.
items.rationale: The banned password vocabulary list is a documented design policy.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that, if the application includes multiple authentication pathways, these are all documented
items.rationale: Documenting auth pathways is a direct architectural design requirement.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that either a multi-factor authentication mechanism or a combination of single-factor authentication mechanisms, must be used
items.rationale: The requirement to implement MFA is a high-level architectural mandate.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that a secure process for resetting a forgotten password is implemented, that does not bypass any enabled multi-factor authentication mechanisms.
items.rationale: The architecture of the recovery flow is designed and verified via a TSD.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the user’s session inactivity timeout and absolute maximum session lifetime are documented
items.rationale: Session timeout lengths are documented policies in a specification.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the documentation defines how many concurrent (parallel) sessions are allowed for one account
items.rationale: Concurrent session limits are architectural policies defined in a TSD.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that all systems that create and manage user sessions as part of a federated identity management ecosystem... are documented
items.rationale: Federated identity architecture and session lifetimes must be mapped out in a TSD.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application performs all session token verification using a trusted, backend service.
items.rationale: Architectural placement of session verification (backend vs frontend) is a design choice.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application gives the option to terminate all other active sessions after a successful change or removal of any authentication factor
items.rationale: Offering global session termination is a systemic feature/design capability.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that authorization documentation defines rules for restricting function-level and data-specific access
items.rationale: The authorization model and its rules are explicitly TSD documents.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application’s documentation defines the environmental and contextual attributes... used to make security decisions
items.rationale: Defining context-aware access attributes (time, IP) is an architectural policy.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application ensures that function-level access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions.
items.rationale: Function-level access control requires a defined RBAC/ABAC model in the architecture.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that tokens are only sent to components that strictly need them.
items.rationale: Data flow architecture dictates where tokens are transmitted.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that refresh tokens and reference access tokens can be revoked by an authorized user using the authorization server user interface
items.rationale: Providing a token revocation UI is a high-level systemic feature design.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that for each service the application uses, the documentation defines the maximum number of concurrent connections
items.rationale: Documenting connection pool limits is a TSD-level architectural requirement.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that all sensitive data created and processed by the application has been identified and classified into protection levels.
items.rationale: Data classification and setting protection boundaries is a fundamental architectural requirement verifiable in a TSD.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that sensitive information is subject to data retention classification, ensuring that outdated or unnecessary data is deleted
items.rationale: Data retention rules are business logic policies defined during the design phase.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application documentation identifies functionality which is time-consuming or resource-demanding.
items.rationale: Threat modeling and identifying resource limits is documented in the design/architecture.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that an inventory exists documenting the logging performed at each layer of the application’s technology stack
items.rationale: Designing the logging architecture and inventorying telemetry points is a TSD activity.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that input is decoded or unescaped into a canonical form only once... and that this is done before processing the input further
items.rationale: Verifying the exact order of decoding vs sanitization operations requires source code inspection.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application performs output encoding and escaping either as a final step before being used by the interpreter
items.rationale: Checking if encoding happens as the absolute final step requires reading the code execution flow.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that output encoding for an HTTP response, HTML document, or XML document is relevant for the context required
items.rationale: Context-aware encoding requires verifying specific function calls in the source code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that when dynamically building URLs, untrusted data is encoded according to its context
items.rationale: Verifying URL concatenation and encoding logic requires source code review.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that data selection or database queries (e.g., SQL, HQL, NoSQL, Cypher) use parameterized queries, ORMs, entity frameworks
items.rationale: The exact implementation of parameterized queries requires inspecting the database integration layer in code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application protects against OS command injection and that operating system calls use parameterized OS queries
items.rationale: Validating how OS commands are constructed and executed is a code-level check.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application protects against LDAP injection vulnerabilities
items.rationale: LDAP filter escaping is an implementation detail verified via code analysis.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that all untrusted HTML input from WYSIWYG editors or similar is sanitized using a well-known and secure HTML sanitization library
items.rationale: Verifying the usage and invocation of specific sanitization libraries requires source code review.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application avoids the use of eval() or other dynamic code execution features
items.rationale: Checking for unsafe eval() functions requires scanning the source code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application uses memory-safe string, safer memory copy and pointer arithmetic
items.rationale: Pointer arithmetic and memory management are purely source-code implementation details.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application configures XML parsers to use a restrictive configuration and that unsafe features such as resolving external entities are disabled
items.rationale: XXE prevention requires verifying how the XML parser is initialized in the code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that deserialization of untrusted data enforces safe input handling, such as using an allowlist of object types
items.rationale: Deserialization allowlists are implemented and verified directly within the source code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that input is validated to enforce business or functional expectations for that input. This should either use positive validation against an allow list
items.rationale: Input validation regex and bounds checking logic are verified in code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application will only process business logic flows for the same user in the expected sequential step order and without skipping steps.
items.rationale: Verifying sequential state enforcement requires deep inspection of the logic handlers in code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that anti-automation controls are in place to protect against excessive calls to application functions
items.rationale: Verifying the implementation of rate limiting variables/counters is a code-level activity.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that content intended to be displayed as text, rather than rendered as HTML, is handled using safe rendering functions (such as createTextNode or textContent)
items.rationale: Safe DOM manipulation methods must be verified in the frontend JavaScript source code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that cookies have the ‘Secure’ attribute set, and if the ’__Host-’ prefix is not used for the cookie name, the ’__Secure-’ prefix must be used
items.rationale: Cookie attribute flags and name prefixes are set directly in the application code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that cookies have the ’__Host-’ prefix for the cookie name unless they are explicitly designed to be shared
items.rationale: Validating cookie prefix generation requires code review.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that... requests are validated to ensure they originate from the application itself. This may be done by using and validating anti-forgery tokens
items.rationale: CSRF anti-forgery token generation and validation logic is implemented in code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that messages received by the postMessage interface are discarded if the origin of the message is not trusted
items.rationale: Validating origins in cross-window messaging requires reviewing frontend JS listeners.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that, if the application... builds and sends requests, it uses validation, sanitization, or other mechanisms to avoid creating URIs... which are too long
items.rationale: String length validation before sending external requests is a code-level defense.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that a query allowlist, depth limiting, amount limiting, or query cost analysis is used to prevent GraphQL... Denial of Service (DoS)
items.rationale: GraphQL depth limit configuration logic sits within the application source code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that when the application creates file paths for file operations... it uses internally generated or trusted data
items.rationale: Preventing path traversal requires analyzing file I/O concatenation in code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application validates or ignores user-submitted filenames
items.rationale: Filename sanitization functions are validated via source code analysis.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that controls to prevent attacks such as credential stuffing and password brute force are implemented according to the application’s security documentation.
items.rationale: Verifying the actual implementation logic of credential stuffing controls requires code review.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that system generated initial passwords or activation codes are securely randomly generated
items.rationale: Randomness implementation and entropy checks are code-level verifications.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that lookup secrets, out-of-band authentication requests or codes, and time-based one-time passwords (TOTPs) are only successfully usable once.
items.rationale: Verifying state invalidation for single-use secrets requires reading the application logic.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that, when being stored in the application’s backend, lookup secrets... are hashed with an approved password storage hashing algorithm that incorporates a 32-bit random salt.
items.rationale: Verifying the salt size and hashing algorithm requires reviewing cryptographic functions in code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that if reference tokens are used to represent user sessions, they are unique and generated using a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG)
items.rationale: Session token generation algorithms must be verified in the source code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application generates a new session token on user authentication, including re-authentication
items.rationale: Session regeneration upon authentication is a specific logic flow tested in code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that there is an inactivity timeout such that re-authentication is enforced according to risk analysis
items.rationale: The technical enforcement of a session timeout requires code inspection.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that when session termination is triggered... the application disallows any further use of the session... invalidating the session data at the application backend.
items.rationale: Ensuring backend invalidation upon logout is verified through code analysis.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application requires full re-authentication before allowing modifications to sensitive account attributes
items.rationale: Protecting specific modification routes requires checking access control logic in code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application ensures that data-specific access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions to specific data items to mitigate insecure direct object reference (IDOR)
items.rationale: IDOR protections require analyzing object ownership checks within the data access code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the application ensures that field-level access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions to specific fields to mitigate broken object property level authorization (BOPLA).
items.rationale: Field-level access (BOPLA) verification requires deep inspection of data mapping code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that multi-tenant applications use cross-tenant controls to ensure consumer operations will never affect tenants with which they do not have permissions
items.rationale: Tenant isolation enforcement requires analyzing the query filters in code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that self-contained tokens are validated using their digital signature or MAC to protect against tampering
items.rationale: JWT signature validation functions must be inspected in source code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that only algorithms on an allowlist can be used to create and verify self-contained tokens... and must not include the ‘None’ algorithm.
items.rationale: Validating JWT algorithms in the library initialization requires code review.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that, if a validity time span is present in the token data, the token and its content are accepted only if the verification time is within this validity time span.
items.rationale: Verifying ‘nbf’ and ‘exp’ JWT claims requires checking the token validation code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the service only accepts tokens which are intended for use with that service (audience). For JWTs, this can be achieved by validating the ‘aud’ claim
items.rationale: Verifying audience claim enforcement requires source code analysis.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the client only accepts values from the authorization server... if these values result from an authorization flow that was initiated by the same user agent
items.rationale: Verifying PKCE or state parameter correlation logic requires code review.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the resource server only accepts access tokens that are intended for use with that service (audience).
items.rationale: OAuth RS audience validation is implemented in the application code layer.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the resource server enforces authorization decisions based on claims from the access token that define delegated authorization.
items.rationale: Access control decisions mapped to claims must be reviewed in code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the authorization server validates redirect URIs based on a client-specific allowlist of pre-registered URIs using exact string comparison.
items.rationale: Exact string comparison for redirect URIs is a code-level implementation detail.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that, if the authorization server returns the authorization code in the authorization response, it can be used only once for a token request.
items.rationale: Authorization code invalidation and state tracking requires source code inspection.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that the client (as the relying party) mitigates ID Token replay attacks. For example, by ensuring that the ‘nonce’ claim in the ID Token matches
items.rationale: OIDC nonce validation requires reviewing the authentication logic in code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that insecure block modes (e.g., ECB) and weak padding schemes (e.g., PKCS#1 v1.5) are not used.
items.rationale: Ensuring bad ciphers/paddings are avoided requires checking cryptographic function arguments in code.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that sensitive data is only sent to the server in the HTTP message body or header fields, and that the URL and query string do not contain sensitive information
items.rationale: Verifying how requests are constructed in the frontend requires source code review.

items.requirement_excerpt: Verify that all logging components appropriately encode data to prevent log injection.
items.rationale: Log sanitization logic is implemented natively in the code.
